source.title: The More Popular, The Harder to Forget: Adaptive Popularity for LLM Unlearning
source.authors: Anna Borisiuk; A. Savchenko; Alexander Panchenko; Elena Tutubalina

page_placements.theme: Target properties and training history set how deeply unlearning works

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests recovery under paraphrased and adversarial prompts and compares internal metrics across unlearning methods. Its results challenge a blanket claim that unlearning only hides knowledge, while finding that recovery and robustness vary by method and setting.
record.gate_note: The paper reports paraphrase and adversarial-prompt results in Table 4, popularity-tier paraphrase results in Table 5, and internal metrics in Table 6. No attack-condition result for an unmodified model is reported, so these results do not directly compare attack recovery with a model that never underwent unlearning. The paper does not test relearning attacks or quantization. A prompt embedded in the text instructs the reader to return a JSON array; it is unrelated to the study and is treated as text addressed to an AI reviewer.
record.test_reason: This does not reproduce an original source. It is a paper introducing a new method, AdaPop, which also reports prompt-attack recovery (DUET paraphrases, RWKU Level-3 adversarial prompts) for GA, GD, NPO and WGA, alongside capability checks (MMLU, HellaSwag) and correlational internal metrics (ΔRank, Hid.Cos). The results show that recovery depends on the method and the attack. Paraphrasing recovers nothing for WGA (Llama, Gemma) or AdaPop. Adversarial prompts recover part of the knowledge for WGA and AdaPop. NPO never removes much to begin with. So the study bears on A, E and F, and, correlationally, on C. The record lacks each method's own direct-query forget score (Tables 1–3), which is the baseline needed to read the attack rows as recovery.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that AdaPop gives the lowest adversarial-query scores among stable methods on all three models and the best paraphrase scores on two (on Llama it is within seed noise of WGA). They claim about 5× less paraphrase leakage and 1.6× less adversarial leakage, and read ΔRank/Hid.Cos as parametric disruption rather than surface suppression. They describe WGA as suppressing only the surface answer, NPO as under-erasing popular facts, and GA/GD as collapsing. General capability stays within 0.05 MMLU.
record.recipe_differences: AdaPop is a new popularity-conditioned unlearning method evaluated against existing unlearning baselines; the paper does not reproduce one of the named original-source methods as its central intervention.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary by method and prompt set: AdaPop is best on paraphrases for two of three models, while it has the lowest adversarial-query score on all three. The reported results also distinguish DUET paraphrase queries from RWKU Level-3 adversarial prompts.

fits_no_version.finding: Popular facts resist unlearning more than rare ones. NPO paraphrase recall on Llama is 0.854 for popular vs 0.538 for rare facts (Table 5). The paper says popular facts need about an order of magnitude more learning rate to forget (§5.2, App. N), though App. O gives 5e-5 vs 1e-4 for Llama.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: How deeply knowledge is unlearned, and how recoverable it is, depends on a fact's pretraining frequency or popularity.

record.problems: The reported prompt-attack table has no no-unlearning or never-trained comparison under the same attack prompts, so it cannot establish whether recovery exceeds that reference. Prompt attack outcomes are reported as ROUGE-L, not targeted-knowledge accuracy. Internal metrics are correlational diagnostics, not causal evidence of deletion. Some baseline near-zero results are confounded by model collapse.
record.rows_left_out: None of the reported Table 4 model-by-method-by-prompt-set outcomes or Table 6 AdaPop/WGA internal metrics were omitted. Other Table 6 methods and unrelated output-quality results were left out because they do not add a distinct recovery or internal-mechanism result needed for the tested versions.

untested.parts: Targeted accuracy vs chance is not measured (only ROUGE-L and cosine are reported). No WMDP-style hazardous knowledge. RMU is evaluated only on output overlap (Appendix H), not under attack.
No activation-direction ablation or causal test; only correlational ΔRank, Hid.Cos and KL metrics.
Results for the nine strategies (jailbreak-like prefix injection, cross-lingual, role-play and others) are pooled. No in-context-information attack. No original-model score on the attack sets.
AdaPop is not tested against relearning, quantization or activation-ablation attacks.

missing.what: Direct-query forget ROUGE-L for each method and for the original model (w/o MU). This is the baseline needed to read Table 4 as recovery, and it includes NPO's high RWKU direct scores (0.271–0.540) used in the A verdict.
Paraphrase recall split by popularity tier. AdaPop is lower than WGA on popular facts; rare facts are near the floor for all stable methods.
MMLU/HellaSwag for GA (chance, 0.23–0.25), GD, NPO and WGA.
Eleven extra methods. RMU and UNDIAL leave DUET forget at 0.73–0.88, i.e. they do not unlearn entity facts.
NPO internal metrics (Hid.Cos 0.861/0.883, ΔRank +8,824/+2,739) and the retain-split ΔRank used for comparison.

record.verdict_notes:
Repair of the quarantined verdict. Every row now has exactly one row_fixes item. Because a row carries one state, each of the 11 duplicated rows is linked only to versions whose reading shares that state. The other reading is stated in the problem text.
- AdaPop DUET rows: A, F (observed). The E reading is 'no recovery'.
- NPO DUET rows: A (absent). The E reading was cannot_determine and is dropped.
- WGA Llama/Gemma DUET rows: E (absent). The A reading is 'unlearning held'.
- NPO RWKU rows: E (observed/partial/observed). The A reading is absent; it is kept via the text in the A challenges reason and in missing.

Labels were adjusted to match:
- AdaPop DUET rows removed from E challenges.
- WGA DUET rows removed from A supports.
- NPO RWKU rows removed from A challenges.
- WGA RWKU rows removed from F limits_scope, since they were never linked to F.

One judgment changed on the text: WGA RWKU and NPO-Qwen RWKU moved from E supports to E limits_scope. Their row states are partial (recovery to about 37–70% of the original's direct score), which overlaps AdaPop's range, already labelled limits_scope. E supports now rests on NPO Llama/Gemma RWKU.

The fits_no_version learning-rate statement was corrected, because the paper is internally inconsistent (order of magnitude in §5.2/App. N; 5e-5 vs 1e-4 in App. O).

Other judgments are unchanged:
- Reader codes V1/V3/V5/V6 are mapped to A/C/E/F.
- Attack-row states use each method's own direct-query score (Tables 1–3) as the baseline and the original's direct score as the ceiling. The paper reports no original-model score on the attack sets, so the recovery fractions are approximate.
- GD's adversarial rises (e.g. 0.026 to 0.254 on Llama) stay cannot_determine because the paper flags GD as collapsed.
- ΔRank is model-averaged, and the retain splits show large negative shifts for all stable methods.
- All runs use LoRA at lr 1e-4 on 7–8B instruct models.

The text contains a line telling a model to reply only with a JSON array. It belongs to the paper's own LLM-judge annotation prompt (Appendix D/E). It was treated as data and not followed.

versions.untested_parts: The study reports output-overlap measures and general-capability results, but does not measure targeted-knowledge accuracy against chance. It tests prompt robustness only with its specified paraphrase and adversarial subsets.
No post-unlearning fine-tuning or relearning attack is reported.
The paper analyzes hidden-state similarity and token-rank changes, but does not ablate an activation direction or establish deletion versus access blocking causally.

Tests paraphrased queries and a Level-3 adversarial subset comprising nine prompt-manipulation strategies. Individual strategy results, including cross-lingual or jailbreak-specific outcomes, are not separately reported.
AdaPop is evaluated against paraphrase and adversarial-prompt recovery, but not against relearning or quantization attacks.

relationships.condition: AdaPop on DUET paraphrases, all three models, with capability checks
relationships.reason: AdaPop paraphrase recall (0.027–0.074) stays at its own direct floor (0.023–0.056; originals 0.89–0.94), and MMLU/HellaSwag stay within 0.05 (T4-L-D-Ada, T4-Q-D-Ada, T4-G-D-Ada, T7 rows). WGA on Llama and Gemma shows the same but is linked to E.
relationships.display_finding: Paraphrase recall stayed at 0.027–0.074 versus direct recall of 0.023–0.056 and original recall of 0.89–0.94, while MMLU and HellaSwag stayed within 0.05 of baseline.
